rationale: Interpreted the over-subscription revision, which refutes the occupancy explanation rather than the defect: with 320 racing calls against 64 slots the post-shutdown strand persisted (2, 3 and 2 of eight calls incomplete), so the buffer is not full when the loop exits and later callers still find a free slot. The account keeps its defect claim and its earlier counts, gains that counterevidence item and a corrected limitation, and the Fact is extended under its own id to record that spare capacity is not the deciding factor. No execution is requested.

knowledge.statement: VerifyLeader can hand back a future that nothing will ever complete, because the request waits in the buffered verifyCh that no reader drains once the run loop has exited and the future itself carries no shutdown channel to unblock on. The trigger does not require racing Shutdown: calls made after Shutdown has already returned strand about half the time. The corrected revision measured 11 of 24 post-shutdown VerifyLeader calls stranded against 0 of 48 for the default unbuffered Barrier and Apply, and with BatchApplyCh - which buffers applyCh - Barrier stranded 11 of 24 and Apply 13 of 24. A later revision over-subscribed verifyCh with 320 concurrent racing calls, five times its 64 slots, and the strand persisted (2, 3 and 2 of eight post-shutdown calls incomplete), so spare capacity at the exit is not what decides it: the surplus senders are released by the shutdown case rather than holding slots.
knowledge.conditions: Single-voter Raft instance, HeartbeatTimeout = ElectionTimeout = LeaderLeaseTimeout = 50ms, in-memory transport in one process, BatchApplyCh off unless stated; 128 or 320 concurrent calls around Shutdown plus eight sequential calls after Shutdown has returned.
knowledge.changed_premise: The premise is unchanged and one proposed explanation is removed: the strand is not conditional on spare capacity in the buffered channel, since over-subscribing it five-fold left the outcome unchanged. The earlier counts stay and the over-subscribed ones are added.

interpretations.rationale: The question is whether a future handed back by VerifyLeader, Barrier or Apply around Shutdown can be left permanently uncompleted, and the corrected revision now answers it with all five declared comparisons satisfied, including the two that a configuration change makes decisive. A call made after Shutdown has returned should get the documented 'raft is already shutdown' error, and that is what happens for the unbuffered call kinds: Barrier and Apply answered all eight post-shutdown calls in every trial (comparisons 2 and 3, indices 3, 9, 15 and 5, 11, 17). VerifyLeader, whose channel is always buffered, answered only 4, 4 and 5 of its eight post-shutdown calls (indices 1, 7 and 13), leaving 4, 4 and 3 futures incomplete after 500ms. With BatchApplyCh enabled - the option whose comment says it buffers applyCh to MaxAppendEntries and thereby breaks the timeout guarantee on Apply - the two unbuffered kinds flip: Barrier answered 6, 3 and 4 of eight (indices 25, 29, 33) and Apply 3, 3 and 5 (indices 27, 31, 35), leaving 11 and 13 of 24 calls stranded respectively, with roughly half of the calls in each case answered and the rest left with a future nothing will complete (comparisons 0 and 1). That is a causal rather than correlational demonstration: the only difference between the answered and the stranded cases is whether the channel a future is sent to is buffered, since the call shape, the future type and the absence of a shutdown channel on these futures are identical. The source explains the split exactly: VerifyLeader and the apply path share the same select over the shutdown channel and a channel send, verifyCh is created with 64 slots while applyCh is unbuffered unless BatchApplyCh buffers it, and none of these futures sets ShutdownCh, so deferError.Error() waits on an error channel that no surviving goroutine will write. The repository's own test file records the same class as a TODO for these calls, which is an admission that the gap was known rather than a contract that permits a caller's Error() to block forever. The earlier receipts stay part of the account: the first showed the racing form, 9 and 41 of 64 futures incomplete in two of three trials with none in the control, and the two later revisions did not reproduce that form (0 of 128 per case), so the racing variant is a timing-dependent manifestation while the post-shutdown form is stable across three executions and is the one the claim rests on. A fifth revision tested whether the strand depends on spare capacity in verifyCh by issuing 320 concurrent racing calls, five times the 64 slots, in three VerifyLeader cases (result events at parsed indices 25, 27 and 29). Over-subscription did not protect later callers: 6, 5 and 6 of the eight post-shutdown calls were answered and 2, 3 and 2 returned futures that stayed incomplete, which is the same outcome as the 128-call cases in the same run (5, 1 and 3 answered; 3, 7 and 5 stranded) and the declared comparison asking for every post-shutdown call to be answered was therefore contradicted with three valid witnesses. The reading is that the racing surplus senders are released by the shutdown case instead of holding slots, so the buffer ends partially empty at the exit and later callers still find a free slot to be accepted into; occupancy at the exit is thus not what decides the strand, and the mechanism stands as the buffered channel plus a future with no shutdown channel of its own.
counterevidence: The racing form did not reproduce in the later revisions (0 of 128 calls per case in two runs), so the earlier 9 and 41 are a timing-dependent manifestation rather than a rate.

Without BatchApplyCh the apply path is never affected: Barrier and Apply answered every post-shutdown call in all three runs (indices 3, 9, 15 and 5, 11, 17 here), so the defect reaches the apply path only under a configuration whose own comment already warns that it breaks the Apply timeout guarantee.

Roughly half of the calls in each affected case are answered with the documented shutdown error rather than stranded, so the outcome is a per-call select choice, and no call that was answered carried a wrong outcome.
The repository's test file records the same class as a known TODO, which is evidence about intent, not a reason to treat an unbounded block as acceptable.

Over-subscribing verifyCh five-fold did not remove the strand: the 320-call cases stranded 2, 3 and 2 of eight post-shutdown calls, against 3, 7 and 5 of eight for the 128-call cases, so the outcome is not decided by spare capacity being available when the loop exits.
limitations: The post-shutdown counts per case come from three trials of eight calls each (VerifyLeader 11 of 24 stranded; batched Barrier 11 of 24; batched Apply 13 of 24), so they bound the mechanism rather than a population rate.
The strand is classified by a 500ms window; permanence is inferred from the source, since no reader of the affected channel remains and these futures carry no shutdown channel.
Single-voter node, in-memory transport, 50ms timeouts, one process: no peer round trip or networked shutdown is involved.

The over-subscribed cases carry 320 concurrent racing calls, five times the 64 verifyCh slots, so a large share of sends could not be accepted; the buffer still ended with free slots and the strand persisted, which means occupancy at the exit is not what the probe controls.
interpretations.joint_history: This receipt is the fourth revision of one harness lineage: b2ccc787c9384b008b5f9c668746f760-experiment (64 calls, 1500ms window) gave the racing form, 49fa455b2fe94d53ab6fed2fad19ce33-experiment (128 calls, 4000ms window, post-shutdown phase) isolated the stable form, 3b7823e321e048b88feb0bab3b79b2bd-experiment added the BatchApplyCh cases, and 9bc3e6d5ea9c4b298e4a229e13b8f86d-experiment gave the batched cases distinct trial identifiers so their setup events admit them unambiguously. Event names, case kinds and field meanings are unchanged across the four. The fifth revision 4916079656954a2b81e3a6bfdb12f816-experiment reuses the same harness, adds over-subscribed VerifyLeader cases and takes the call count as a parameter; event names, case kinds and field meanings are unchanged, so its racing and post-shutdown fields are comparable with the earlier revisions.
